openQuestions.text: Trust, phases 006-approval-grants, 007-per-bot-apps and 008-vault: which reference files implement approval grants, per-bot tool or app filtering and a secret store with injection, what should the builder lift or mirror, and which leak, bypass or precedence bugs did those repos hit that the plan does not guard against?

Net-new and operations: what do the ten reference repos have that neither the 003 build plan nor the skip list of the parity synthesis covers, ranked by value to a small team, and which test corpora, failure-handling patterns and upgrade paths in those repos should feed phases 013-manual-testing-scenarios, 014-skilled-and-doc-alignment and 015-deep-review?
What dedupe window does a transport need when the provider offset resets on restart, and what does the reference's bounded recent-update cache size imply for a durable seen record?
Does the per-run filtered UTCP config compare a tool name before or after normalisation, and can a normalised alias slip past the apps filter?
Which transports can prove a send never left (NotSent reconciliation) from their own error shape, and which must treat every ambiguous result as unknown?
Does a Slack envelope redelivered after reconnect double-answer when the press was already applied, and what acknowledgement order keeps the reply index idempotent?
Which of the four non-override rules does a routine-origin approval need, and does a standing answer saved from a check-in survive the next run?
Does the plan secret-store-unreadable detail ever carry a captured backend message, and what fixed phrase replaces it per cause?
Which button or block label vocabulary does the reference already carry, and does any of it pass a secret-literal check without new text?

resolvedQuestions.text: Human surface, phases 001-activity-and-actor and 002-routine-layer: which reference files implement an activity feed, an inbox, an actor on a record and routines with an until outcome, what should the builder lift or mirror, and which failures or fixes in those repos does the plan not guard against?

openhuman-full, never studied before: what do its five vendored crates (tinyagents, tinyconnectors, tinymemory, tinyhumans-sdk, tinysecurity) and its built openhuman-tui crate hold that openhuman-main lacks, and what does that change for phase 003-terminal-screen and its six children and for any other planned phase?

Phase 011-messaging-channels: which reference files implement a channel adapter seam, Telegram, Slack, Signal and WhatsApp transports, identity linking, a durable queue and approvals rendered as buttons or replies, what should the builder lift or mirror, and which delivery, retry or duplicate-message failures did those repos hit?

Prompt and records, phases 004-computer-exposure, 005-memory, 009-skills and 010-conversations: which reference files implement a working place named in the prompt, shared and per-bot memory with a size bound, a skill list under a cap and an append-only conversation with bot routing, and which pitfalls did those repos hit?

keyFindings.text: **003-terminal-screen, phase 003 child 006 (hardening).** openhuman-full does not carry a TUI crate that openhuman-main lacks: the two `crates/openhuman-tui` trees are the same 432K and their `src/` file lists are identical, and the single README the plan cites from `openhuman-main` is the same file. What openhuman-full adds is the *source* of the twenty-one vendored TinyHumans crates: every `vendor/<crate>` directory under `openhuman-main` is empty (0 bytes) while openhuman-full's `vendor/` is 417M, and openhuman-full's root manifest path-links them (`tinyagents-hooks = { path = "vendor/tinyagents/crates/tinyagents-hooks" }`). The reference evidence for phase 003 therefore comes from the same TUI source the plan already cites; the new material is the vendored crates. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/Cargo.toml:46-47] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/README.md:1-6] (observed)

**006 — OpenBot's standing answer is three exclusions, not a rung.** `offersStandingRule` returns false when `policy.source === "task"`, when `policy.closed === true`, or when `policy.behaviour === "hand_off"`; only then does the card offer "Always allow here" or "Allow for this conversation". A task started from a check-in "asks before every change whatever the person's rules say", so a standing answer saved from one "would be ignored the next time and only mislead". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/standing-rule.ts:21-29] *(observed)* The plan's ladder is four rungs in order — kinds of action, rules, auto-review, extra vigilant — and says nothing about which approvals may take a standing answer. Phase 002's routines raise exactly the check-in-origin case this predicate excludes, so 006 needs the exclusion or a routine's first approval silently becomes permanent. The earlier synthesis carries the rung order only. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/001-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:89]

**Phase 001 — the seven group titles are liftable verbatim and the plan fixes only the ids.** `ACTIVITY_GROUPS` declares each group as `{ id, title }` in one ordered array: `needs_you`/"Needs you", `working`/"Working", `scheduled`/"Scheduled", `done`/"Done", `stopped`/"Stopped", `failed`/"Failed", `recurring`/"Recurring" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/bot-lifecycle/activity-groups.ts:28-39]. Phase 001's REQ-001 fixes the seven ids and their order and REQ-002 requires each group to carry a `title`, but no line in the phase fixes the title strings, so a builder invents seven labels that the screen's sample payload then has to match. Lift the array as-is under the MIT notice REQ-006 already requires. (observed)

**The plan drops the reference's mid-poll webhook recovery, so a webhook set after start wedges the Telegram poller.** The reference clears a webhook twice: once before the first poll, and again *inside* the poll loop when `getUpdates` answers 409 whose description contains "webhook" — it calls `deleteWebhook` and `continue`s into a fresh poll with no backoff. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/providers/telegram/channel_ops.rs:1936-1952] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/providers/telegram/channel_core.rs:267-272] The plan clears the webhook only in the `listen` start sequence, then says "a `409` from Telegram waits 2 s and polls again". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/005-polling-transports/spec.md:212] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/005-polling-transports/spec.md:99] A 409 is not always "another poller": it is also "can't use getUpdates while webhook is active", a state anything that sets a webhook later can produce. Waiting 2 s against that condition never converges. **Observed** on both sides. The evidence supports the reference: the plan needs the in-loop branch, with the same discriminator (does the description name a webhook) so a genuine second-poller 409 still backs off rather than calling `deleteWebhook` in a loop.

**006 — the bot-voice leak has a test shape the plan lacks.** Every sentence the server answers a step with is exported from one file, and "`server/tests/approval-outcomes-for-person.test.ts` walks these exports and the approval service's, and fails on any that a person would still read in the words written for the Bot, so a sentence added later cannot leak by being forgotten here". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/approval-outcomes.ts:12-16] *(observed)* The plan's 006 adds a grant and a ladder and no test that a person-facing string is not written in the bot's voice. Phase 012 owns the scenario; the export-and-walk test belongs to 006.

**006 — OpenBot classifies a decision by the tool left waiting, not by the action's verb.** `DECISION_TOOLS` maps `askApproval` to `approval` and `askChoice` and `askForm` to `question`, and the server "watches runs for a call to one that is left waiting, which is what puts the Bot under Needs you". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/decision-tools.ts:13-17] *(observed)* The plan's 006 adds an `action-kind.ts` that classifies the action. The two disagree on what makes an item a needs-you item: OpenBot counts a waiting decision tool, the plan counts an action kind. The evidence supports keeping both — the action kind for the grant, the waiting tool for the count — and the plan should say so, because a run that asks with a plain question would otherwise not appear under needs-you.

**007 and 008 — the token compare to mirror is length-first and branch-free.** `matchesToken` returns false on an empty expected value or a length mismatch, then XOR-accumulates every code unit and compares the accumulator to zero. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/agent-authorisation.ts:2-9] *(observed)* The plan's REQ-011 already requires a constant-time read-back compare [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/008-vault/spec.md:165], so this adds the shape rather than the requirement.

**Evidence limit — the OpenBot snapshot has no `server/`, so the ladder's lower rungs are readable only as prose.** `shared/standing-rule.ts` cites `server/src/approvals/policy.ts`, `service.ts` and `store.ts`, and `shared/decision-tools.ts` cites `server/src/approvals/decision-waits.ts`; none of those paths exists in the vendored tree. `shared/sensitive-rule.test.ts` is present with no `shared/sensitive-rule.ts` beside it. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/standing-rule.ts:6-8] *(observed)* Rungs 2 to 4 of the plan's ladder therefore rest on `docs/approvals.md` alone, and the plan's own handoff criterion already marks them not implemented in this phase. Any later phase that implements rung 2 needs a different reference than this snapshot.

**003-terminal-screen, child 006-hardening-and-proof.** The TUI treats terminal ownership as a panic-safe invariant, not as a normal-exit concern: its module doc says alternate screen and raw mode "**must** be undone on every exit path — normal return, `?` propagation, and panic — or the user's shell is left in a broken state (no echo, no line editing, stuck on the alternate screen)", a `TerminalGuard` restores on `Drop`, and `install_panic_hook` chains `restore` ahead of the previous hook so the backtrace prints to a sane terminal. `restore` itself is ordinary crossterm teardown (`LeaveAlternateScreen`, `disable_raw_mode`), and a failed restore is logged rather than propagated. The 003 plan's hardening child requires `cargo fmt`, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test` and a release `pty_smoke` run; no line of it requires a panic hook or a restore-on-drop, so a panic in the render loop is a failure the plan does not guard against, and the pty smoke test would pass while a panicking frame still leaves the operator's terminal in raw mode. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/terminal.rs:1-8] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/terminal.rs:104-118] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/terminal.rs:90-102] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/006-hardening-and-proof/spec.md:140-156] (observed, and the gap is inferred from the plan's requirement list)

**006 — a grant may convert a required approval into an automatic one and may override nothing else.** `ApprovalGrants2` carries "exact tool names, and exact tool names inside one named flow"; a grant "only converts a required approval into an automatic one (`auto:tool-grant`, `auto:flow-grant`)" and "never overrides a denial, a Cron external effect, reviewed reuse or a human-only tool (`HUMAN_ONLY_TOOLS2`, `native_*`)". "Names are never wildcards." [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinysecurity/docs/module-approval-contracts.md:35-41] *(observed)* This is the missing half of the plan's ladder: the plan records the order in which a decision is reached but not the four things a grant may not reach past. A builder writing `grants` on a needs-you item needs the non-override list as a field-level rule, not as prose.

**A deduplicated Telegram update must still advance the offset, and the reference has a test for exactly that; the plan's offset rule does not say it.** The reference advances `offset` on the seen path before `continue`ing. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/providers/telegram/channel_ops.rs:1967-1971] The named test is `a_deduplicated_update_still_advances_the_offset`, asserting the second poll carries offset 21 after a duplicate of update 20. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/providers/telegram/channel_ops_tests.rs:3736-3775] The plan states only "The offset moves past an update only after the seen record is written". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/005-polling-transports/spec.md:145] That phrasing is satisfied by "seen record already existed, so skip" — which leaves the offset pinned and re-fetches the same update forever. **Observed.** The evidence supports the reference; the plan's REQ-009 should gain the duplicate-path clause and its acceptance criteria should mirror this test.

**Phase 001 — `stopped` is a derived predicate over a stop instant, not a status value.** The reference never stores a "stopped" status: `stoppedByYou` returns `task?.status === "failed" && Boolean(task.stoppedAt)` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/tasks/queries.ts:300-304], and `taskGroup` routes a failed task to `stopped` or `failed` on that predicate alone [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/bot-lifecycle/activity-groups.ts:82-87]. The 003 synthesis already carries the gap that `stopped` has no data source (003-plan-depth-research §4.001 gap 1); what is new is the shape of the fix — one nullable `stoppedAt` instant on the run record plus a predicate, so no new status value, no index column and no `SCHEMA_VERSION` move, which is exactly the constraint 001's own risk table imposes. (observed for the reference; inferred for the plan's fix shape)

**003-terminal-screen, child 004-panes.** openhuman-tui bounds every tool-output string in the reducer rather than at the draw call, and it marks the cut: `bounded(value, limit)` sanitizes, returns early when the length fits, walks back to a char boundary (`while !safe.is_char_boundary(end) { end -= 1 }`), and appends `\n[preview truncated]`. The plan clips by display width in `view/panes.rs` (REQ-021) and its mockups show a clipped too-small message, but no requirement in the phase names a marker for a clipped runtime string, so a clipped question reads as a complete one. The reference's char-boundary walk is the part to mirror: a byte-slice clip of a multi-byte question panics, and the plan's clip is display-width based only in `view/panes.rs`, which is a different code path from the answer overlay in child 005. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/activity.rs:207-215] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/004-panes/spec.md:160] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/001-ux-and-component-map/design/mockups.md:2084] (observed, gap inferred)

**006 — a flow grant is weaker than a tool grant for an effect the module cannot label.** For the `Unlabelled` row, a whole-tool grant approves it as an audited `auto:tool-grant`, but "neither `auto_approve_all` nor a flow grant approves it". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinysecurity/docs/module-approval-contracts.md:91] *(observed)* The plan's ladder is a single ordered list, so it cannot express a grant whose strength depends on the effect class. If 006 keeps one ladder, it must at least record that a flow-scoped grant does not cover an unclassified action.

**Phase 001 — the reference dedupes a needs-you item against the run that raised it, and the plan does not.** `groupActivity` skips an approval or question whose `channelId` is one of the listed task's conversations, so it is shown once, as the task [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/app/src/lib/bot-lifecycle/activity-groups.ts:147-152]. Phase 001 sources `needs_you` from the status index and `working` from the bot's held lease side file [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:143], and a parked run holds its lease while its item is open, so one parked run prints twice: once under `needs_you` and once under `working`. The plan needs one dedupe rule keyed on the item's `runId`, which REQ-003 already carries. (observed for the reference; inferred for the plan's absence)

**The reference commits the offset after the provider action succeeds, not after the seen record is written; the plan's wording admits a crash window that loses a message.** The reference marks the update acknowledged locally "only after its provider-owned action or typed ingress has succeeded", and both `track_update_id` and the offset bump happen inside that closure. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/providers/telegram/channel_ops.rs:1973-1981] Under the plan's wording, a crash between writing the seen record and handing the message to the runtime counts as consumed: the offset has moved, the message is gone. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/005-polling-transports/spec.md:145] **Observed (reference) / inferred (plan's implementation risk).** The evidence supports the reference's ordering; the seen write should be the *last* step of ingest, or the offset should be derived from a record that is written after ingest commits.

**003-terminal-screen, child 003-shell-and-navigation.** The reference's loop is fully parameterised and coalesced: `event::poll(Duration::from_millis(100))` for input, a `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_millis(120))` spinner ticker, and a redraw gated on `dirty && last_draw.elapsed() >= Duration::from_millis(16)` so a burst of events draws once per frame. The 003 plan polls its verbs on a 5-second timer and redraws per event, and no child names a coalescing rule or an input poll timeout, so a key repeat storm redraws per key. The reference's 100 ms/16 ms pair is the cheap part to mirror; its 120 ms spinner belongs to a streaming transcript the plan's chat tab does not have yet. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/app.rs:115] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/app.rs:130-147] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/app.rs:188-189] (observed, plan gap inferred)

**006 and 007 — a widening change must re-ask a human, and only a human answer counts.** `SupersedePolicy` returns `ReviewRequired` when the replacement "widens authority (new or broader roots, removed restrictions, new hosts or tools, higher command autonomy, classes, allowlist entries or budget ... new auto origins, judge enabled, enforcement or the registered path scope disabled, or privacy loosened)", and "Only a row decided by an authenticated human qualifies; automatic, judge and reused approvals are refused. A narrowing change activates without review." [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinysecurity/docs/module-subject-policies.md:34-44] *(observed)* Phase 007's `apps:` key is a widening surface: adding a server to `apps:` grants a bot a capability it did not have. The plan's 007 has `apps-unknown-server` for a name that is not a known server, and no rule that a widened `apps:` list re-asks. The evidence supports adding one.

**Phase 001 — the reference drops an action's first row when its failure row is loaded beside it, and the plan has no retry rule.** `oneRowPerAction` collects the `attempt` ids of failed, stopped and refused actions and filters out the matching `computer.action_allowed` row, because "the first is the one a reader believes" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/activity-rows.ts:70-96]. The runtime's queue retries a claimed request up to three times, so one request can leave more than one run record, and `bots activity` has no rule for which of them it prints. The reference's rule is the liftable one: the terminal row wins and the earlier row is left out of the read, not out of the trail. (observed)

**The plan collapses two distinct send-failure states into one `unknown` and therefore never retries a send that provably never started.** The reference carries three recovery states: `SendAttemptStarted` (marked before the platform I/O), `UnknownAfterSend` (an attempt reached the platform and the outcome is unknown), and nothing (a fresh entry). [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/delivery/queue.rs:79-90] Its drain routes both non-empty states into a reconciliation path that asks the handler for an `UnknownSendReconciliation` — `Sent` (ack), `NotSent` (retry), `Unresolved` (leave pending, log) — instead of resending blindly. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/delivery/queue.rs:190-240] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/delivery/types.rs:23-29] The plan's rule is one state: "a `sending` entry found at the start of a drain becomes `unknown`", and `unknown` is never retried. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/004-approval-index-and-send-queue/spec.md:130] That is correct at-most-once behaviour for `UnknownAfterSend`, and wrong for a process that died before issuing the HTTP request: the notice is never delivered and never retried, and the plan records it only as `unknown`. **Observed.** The evidence supports a two-state split with the reconciliation port: `send-attempt-started` is marked before the I/O, `unknown-after-send` is set when an attempt returned an ambiguous error, and only the second one is unretryable. The plan's handoff criteria ("an uncertain send is never retried") is satisfied by that split and by nothing less.

**003-terminal-screen, child 004-panes.** The sanitizer the plan cites is a *filter*, and the plan's rule is a *replacement*, so the two differ in a way a test would catch: `safe_text` drops every control character except `
` (`filter(|ch| !ch.is_control() || *ch == '
')`), while the plan replaces each control character, line breaks included, with `?`. The plan's choice is the one the evidence supports for a one-line row — a kept `
` inside a fixed-height row either corrupts the frame or is silently drawn as a space — and it is already recorded as the single sanitizer rule in `004-panes` REQ-021. What is new here is that the reference's behaviour is not copyable as written, because it keeps newlines by design: its rows are multi-line transcript blocks, and the plan's rows are single-line. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/theme.rs:88-93] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/004-panes/spec.md:160] (observed; the plan-versus-reference reading is inferred)

**008 — tinysecurity is GPL-3.0, so its contract text may be read and never copied.** The vendored crate's licence is "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinysecurity/LICENSE:1-2] *(observed)* The plan lifts only rakazo, which is Apache-2.0. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/rakazo-main/LICENSE:1-2] *(observed)* The plan is therefore right to leave tinysecurity out of `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, but a builder who reads findings 2 to 4 above must restate the rules in the plan's own words. This is the one licence hazard in the trust slice and no earlier synthesis names it.

**Phase 002 — the reference frames a firing in three sentences because a live firing read its own instruction as a routine-management question, did nothing, and recorded `succeeded`.** `FIRING_FRAME` is three fixed sentences: that this is a scheduled firing happening now, that the work belongs in this turn, and that managing routines is not what was asked [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/routine-firing.ts:9-13]. The comment records the failure verbatim: the instruction "Every run, append the current date and time …" was sent as the turn's user message, the model called `list_routines`, found a routine that already said that, answered that it was already configured, and appended nothing — "a routine telling somebody it is working while doing nothing at all, which is worse than one that breaks" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/routine-firing.ts:18-34]. Phase 002 changes when a bot runs and when it stops and never what the run is told: a search of its spec for `firing`, `frame` or `prompt` finds no framing rule. This is the highest-value lift in the phase, it is MIT, and the plan does not guard against the failure at all. (observed)

**The reference's approval surface is text-only and fail-closed, so the plan's button forms have no reference implementation to mirror.** The whole prompt vocabulary is `"Reply \`yes\` to approve or \`no\` to deny."`, and the surface is gated on the channel capability `chat_approvals`. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/approvals/mod.rs:20-26] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/approvals/mod.rs:44-52] When no reply context was recorded for a conversation, `surface()` returns `NoReplyContext` and the parked call "will time out denied". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/approvals/mod.rs:54-60] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/approvals/mod.rs:110-125] The plan's M02 and M04 rows design button forms for `telegram` and `slack` only, with the text forms M01 and M03 on the other three. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/001-channel-ux-and-message-map/design/message-catalog.md:44] [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/001-channel-ux-and-message-map/design/message-catalog.md:46] **Observed.** Two consequences the plan does not record: (a) the only callback machinery to lift is the reference's `acknowledge_callback` plus `callback_is_allowed` pair, which acknowledges the callback query before the item is resolved [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/tinychannels-main/src/providers/telegram/channel_ops.rs:1978-1990]; acknowledging first means a crash after the ack loses the press, which is the opposite of the plan's index-first ordering and is worth a sentence in child 004's ordering decision. (b) The reference's fail-closed `NoReplyContext` is the failure the plan already answers better — its REQ-006 makes a press with no index entry fall through to `answerItem` rather than denying the parked call. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/011-messaging-channels/004-approval-index-and-send-queue/spec.md:128]

**006-approval-grants, 007-per-bot-apps, 008-vault.** The vendored `tinysecurity` workspace (288,030 `.rs` lines, GPL-3.0-only) is the only reference in the corpus with an approval engine, and it answers the question the plan defers: it carries a four-way decision `ApprovalChoice2 { Once, Tool, Flow, Deny }` — `Tool` is "exactly this reviewed tool and content in the same bound context" and `Flow` is "exactly reviewed content in the same flow" — which is the shape behind OpenBot's "allow for this conversation" and "always allow here". The plan refuses both as `grant-scope-unsupported` and defers the rules store to a later packet, and its own risk row argues that refusal is the honest answer because a standing allow with no store is a lie. The reference supports the refusal on size, but it adds two guards the plan does not name: an approval request carries a TTL capped per origin at 180,000 ms for `Copilot`/`SubAgent` and 600,000 ms otherwise, and a *human-only* tool is barred from the automatic path however it is named (`judge_barred` returns true for `binding::is_native(tool)` or a `HUMAN_ONLY_TOOLS2` member). A plan with an unbounded "expired" item has no maximum age, and a later phase that adds any per-bot app grant inherits the need for both.
